title: Sedgwick County, KS Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due
content:
Sedgwick County, KS Property Tax Guide: Offices, Appeals and Selling With Tax Due

Cash Home Buyers in Kansas
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Inherited, behind on payments, tenants, repairs: we buy it as-is
  • Zero fees, zero commissions, zero closing costs
  • No obligation: turn the offer down and owe us nothing

Selling in Sedgwick County? Get a Cash Offer

We buy Sedgwick County houses as-is and reply with a written cash offer.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Kansas statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Sedgwick County, Kansas property tax involves the county assessment office and the county treasurer. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who to contact in Sedgwick County

  • Sedgwick County Treasurer bills and collects the tax and handles delinquent tax.
  • Sedgwick County Appraiser handles assessment and appeals.

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Tax calendar: county mails valuation notices March 1 (K.S.A. 79-1460); equalization appeal due 30 days from notice mailing date (79-1448); informal meeting with County Appraiser by May 15; Hearing Officer/Panel hearings by July 1 (79-1606)
  • Full or first half due December 20; second half due May 10 of the following year; interest charged if December 20 is missed
  • Late interest on real property (K.S.A. 79-2004) for 2017 and after is the K.S.A. 79-2968 prescribed rate plus five percentage points; page's personal-property rate table lists 2025 9% and 2026 8%
  • Unpaid delinquent personal property tax blocks vehicle tag renewal
  • Appeal of valuation notice due 30 days from date county mailed notice (K.S.A. 79-1448); informal meeting by May 15; hearing officer/panel hearings by July 1; then 30 days from informal/panel decision to file with state tax appeals/small claims (page labels it Small Claims Division, 79-1606)

Assessment appeals

Owners can appeal to the county appraiser, then the county hearing panel or board of equalization and the Kansas Board of Tax Appeals. Confirm the current deadline on your county page. See the Kansas property tax guide.

Tax rate

We could not confirm a current county rate on an opened official page. Kansas bills combine county, municipal and school district levies.

Selling in Sedgwick County?
We buy Sedgwick County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Treasurer office hours not on page scraped
  • Current 2026 real property interest percentage (formula plus 5 points; exact figure not shown for real property)
  • Register of Deeds not researched (not required)

How to sell a house in Sedgwick County

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the probate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Kansas.

What a cash sale of a Sedgwick County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Sedgwick County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Kansas disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Sedgwick County

  • Ask the tax collector what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Kansas change, so confirm details with the official office or a Kansas attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Sedgwick County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Sedgwick County property tax guide FAQ

Who handles assessment appeals in Sedgwick County?

Appeals go to the county appraiser, then the county board, then the Kansas Board of Tax Appeals.

What happens to unpaid Sedgwick County property tax when I sell?

The title company pays unpaid tax from the sale proceeds at closing.

Last updated November 14, 2026. Citations come from Kansas statutes and official agency pages linked in Sources. Where we could not confirm something on an official page, we say so.

Sumner County, Kansas property tax involves the county assessment office and the county treasurer. This guide lists what we confirmed on official pages.

Who to contact in Sumner County

  • Sumner County Treasurer bills and collects the tax and handles delinquent tax.
  • Sumner County Appraiser handles assessment and appeals.

What we confirmed on official pages

  • Tax calendar: valuation notices mailed Mar 1; deadline to file real property appeals Mar 30; informal conferences done by May 15; decisions mailed by May 20
  • Dec 20 first half payment-under-protest due; May 10 second half protest payment deadline
  • 1st half taxes due 12/20; 2nd half due May 10; no extension granted
  • Online payment needs tax statement ID/number; 2.5% credit card fee charged by third-party vendor, not county
  • Satellite hours 3rd of each month 9am-3:30pm at Caldwell Workspace, 110 S Main, Caldwell KS
  • Deadline to file real property appeals March 30 (2026 calendar page); personal property appeals May 15

Assessment appeals

Owners can appeal to the county appraiser, then the county hearing panel or board of equalization and the Kansas Board of Tax Appeals. Confirm the current deadline on your county page. See the Kansas property tax guide.

Tax rate

We could not confirm a current county rate on an opened official page. Kansas bills combine county, municipal and school district levies.

Selling in Sumner County?
We buy Sumner County houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

What we could not confirm

  • Street address of Wellington treasurer office not captured

How to sell a house in Sumner County

  1. Find out what the title company needs. For an inherited or transferred house, that usually means the recorded deed or the probate paperwork that shows who owns it today.
  2. Get a payoff for any mortgage and the amount of any unpaid property tax. Both are paid from the sale proceeds at closing.
  3. Compare offers on what you net after repairs, commissions and closing costs, not on the headline price.
  4. If you want a fast, simple closing, ask for a written cash offer. We buy houses as-is, with no repairs and no agent commission. See we buy houses in Kansas.

What a cash sale of a Sumner County house looks like, step by step

People often ask what actually happens after they contact a cash buyer. Here is the usual order of events for a house in Sumner County.

  1. Tell us about the property. Use the form on this page or call or text (424) 435-2326. We ask about the address, the condition and what is going on, such as a mortgage, back taxes, tenants or an estate.
  2. Get a written cash offer. We review the details and send a written offer. There is no obligation, and you can turn it down and owe us nothing.
  3. Pick your closing date. You choose the timeline. Some owners need weeks to move out, and others want to close quickly.
  4. The title company handles the paperwork. It checks ownership, pays off any mortgage and any unpaid property tax from the proceeds, and records the deed.
  5. You receive the proceeds. Our offers carry no agent commission, no fees and no closing costs to you.

Documents and information to have ready

You do not need everything below to get an offer, but each item makes the sale smoother and helps the title company work faster.

  • The deed or other proof of who owns the property today.
  • A recent mortgage statement or a payoff figure from the lender.
  • The latest property tax bill, plus any notice of unpaid or delinquent tax.
  • Homeowners association details, including dues and any unpaid assessments, if there is an association.
  • Current leases and the tenants' contact information, if the house is rented.
  • Estate paperwork, such as letters from the court, if you inherited the house.
  • A short list of known repairs. We buy as-is, but honest information avoids surprises.

Listing, selling it yourself or a cash offer: how they compare

Listing with an agent can bring a higher headline price when a house is in good shape and you have time. You pay the commission agreed in your listing contract, and you usually handle repairs, showings and the buyer's inspection requests. Closing depends on the buyer's financing.

Selling it yourself saves the listing commission but puts the marketing, the paperwork and the required Kansas disclosures on you. You still need a title company or attorney to close.

Taking a cash offer trades some of the headline price for speed and certainty. We buy as-is, so there are no repairs, no showings and no financing contingency. It tends to fit owners dealing with foreclosure pressure, an inherited house, back taxes, tenants or a move on a deadline. Compare every option on what you net after repairs, fees and carrying costs, not on the headline price.

Questions to ask before you sell in Sumner County

  • Ask the tax collector what is owed and what the title company will need at closing.
  • Ask your lender for a written payoff figure good through your expected closing date, and ask whether there is a prepayment penalty.
  • Ask the county assessor whether a pending appeal or exemption affects the bill, and whether any exemption you receive ends when you sell.
  • If the house was inherited, ask the title company which court documents it needs before it will insure the sale.
  • If tenants live in the house, check the lease for its end date and any notice you must give.

These are general questions to start a conversation, not legal advice. Rules in Kansas change, so confirm details with the official office or a Kansas attorney or tax professional.

More questions about selling in Sumner County

How fast can I close on a cash sale?

You choose the closing date within what the title company needs to clear ownership and payoffs.

Do I have to clean out or repair the house?

No. We buy houses as-is, so you do not need to make repairs before selling.

Will you buy a house that has tenants in it?

Yes. We buy rentals as-is, occupied or vacant. Tell us about the lease when you request an offer.

What if I owe more on the mortgage than the house is worth?

Tell us the payoff figure. A sale that does not cover the loan may need lender approval, so ask your lender about a short sale before you sign anything.

Can I sell an inherited house before probate is finished?

It depends on who has legal authority to sign. The title company can tell you what court paperwork it needs.

Is there any cost to request an offer?

No. Requesting an offer is free and carries no obligation.

Sumner County property tax guide FAQ

Who handles assessment appeals in Sumner County?

Appeals go to the county appraiser, then the county board, then the Kansas Board of Tax Appeals.

What happens to unpaid Sumner County property tax when I sell?

The title company pays unpaid tax from the sale proceeds at closing.
